Closed forms for the constants in the odd-weight identities
between dihedral modular graph functions
Noah Schittenhelm
Hack-Nation 2026, Team Ninja Turtles
Preprint, October 2026

Abstract We consider the combinations Xw of twoloop dihedral modular graph functions C(a, b, c) of odd
weight w whose hyperbolic Laplacian is a multiple of
the Eisenstein series E(w). For the odd weights 3 ≤
w ≤ 61 we prove Xw = fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) with fw =
3((w − 1)/2)!/w and gw = 6|Bw−1 |/((w − 1)/2)!. The
proof uses exact Laplace algebra and a harmonicity,
invariance and growth argument. The constant is the
τ20 term of a Laurent polynomial, evaluated in rational
arithmetic. It assumes a theorem of D’Hoker–Kaidi
and a standard lemma, neither checked by code. We
also show exactly that for 3 ≤ w ≤ 25 the space of
combinations with ∆X ∈ QE(w) has dimension 1 for
odd w and 0 for even w. Independently of the proof,
relations at w = 3, . . . , 17 are confirmed numerically
at the working precision of 32 digits at verifier-chosen
points; w = 17 was a preregistered blind test. The full
weight-11 basis has exactly one relation, established
numerically by a singular-value criterion.

Contribution. The Laurent polynomial of each
single Cu,v;w is known (Theorem 5.1 of D’Hoker–Kaidi,
arXiv:1902.04180). We evaluate it in rational arithmetic
on the DGV combinations. This gives closed forms for
fw and gw with a proof for odd w ≤ 61, together with
numerical confirmations independent of that proof.
Summary of results.
• Theorem 1 shows Xw = fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) exactly
for the odd weights 3 ≤ w ≤ 61, with fw and gw
in closed form. The proof is computer-assisted in
rational arithmetic and its assumptions are stated
openly.
• Theorem 2 shows that the space {X : ∆X ∈
QE(w)} is one-dimensional for odd w and zero
for even w, for 3 ≤ w ≤ 25, and is spanned by Xw
for odd w.

Keywords Modular graph functions · Laplace eigenvalue equations · Eisenstein series · Bernoulli numbers ·
Genus-one string amplitudes · Computer-assisted proof

• Observations 1 to 3 confirm numerically, independently of the proof, the constants at w = 3, . . . , 17,
and show that the full weight-11 basis carries exactly one relation. A hardening run exposed and
fixed one evaluator bug.

1 Introduction
Two-loop dihedral modular graph functions C(a, b, c)
appear as coefficients in the low-energy expansion of
the one-loop amplitude of closed strings. D’Hoker,
Green and Vanhove showed that they satisfy Laplace
eigenvalue equations with inhomogeneous terms polynomial in non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, and that
the Laplace equation fixes an algebraic identity only up
to an additive constant of integration [1]. They give
a combination Xw of C(a, b, c) for odd weight whose
Laplacian is proportional to E(w),. The constant g7
was later given in a general procedure based on Laurent
polynomials [2]. Identities among two-loop graphs at
all weights were also constructed earlier [3], and relations between graphs with four and five links have been
proved [4].
Open question. What are the closed forms of fw
and gw in Xw = fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) for odd w?
Difficulty. The Laplace equation alone leaves gw
undetermined [1]. Fixing it requires the Laurent polynomial of each C(a, b, c) at the cusp. The number of
graphs, and with it the size of the combination, grows
with w. Numerical searches for relations among many

Proof. The proof has three steps, following,.

Certificate. The algebraic Laplace representation of
D’Hoker–Green–Vanhove was re-derived and the linear
conditions were solved in exact rational arithmetic for
each w in the range. □
Novelty status: partly known.

1. Since ∆E(w) = w(w −1)E(w), the difference Xw −
fw E(w) is harmonic.
2. The difference is SL(2, Z)-invariant and of polynomial growth at the cusp, hence constant by the standard argument used by D’Hoker–Green–Vanhove.
3. The constant equals the τ20 term of the Laurent
polynomial of Xw . This polynomial follows from
Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 5.1 of D’Hoker–Kaidi
(arXiv:1902.04180), evaluated in rational arithmetic. The transcription was checked against their
eq. (5.19), and the Laurent terms not involving products of zeta values agree with those of
fw E(w) + gw ζ(w); this is a consistency check. The
τ20 term equals gw ζ(w) with gw as stated.

Remark 1 (Conjecture 1). The closed forms fw and gw
of Theorem 1 extend beyond w = 61. Before the proof,
the formula was a conjecture read off from w = 3, . . . , 13.
It is now proved for odd w ≤ 61. A proof for general
odd w is open.
Remark 2 (Status of the computer-assisted parts). The
trusted base consists of exact rational arithmetic in
the Laplace algebra and in the Laurent polynomials
of Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:1902.04180, plus the two assumptions listed in the proof of Theorem 1. In the
numerical observations the base is 32-digit arithmetic at
the verifier-chosen points, together with an exact check
of the leading Laurent coefficient. A third party re-runs
every certificate with the repository commands listed
in the Declarations.

Assumptions not checked by code: the correctness
of Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:1902.04180, proved there in
Appendix A, whose conjectural part concerns only the
coefficient of τ22−w and is not used here, and the standard lemma in step 2. □
Novelty status: partly known. Not given there are
the closed forms for general odd w and their proof. The
Laurent polynomial of each single Cu,v;w is used here
as a tool.
